q: A company moves its on-premises file server to a virtual machine in Azure. Which security task still belongs to the company after the move?
why: On IaaS the customer manages the guest operating system and everything above it, so patching is still theirs. The datacenter, cabling and host hardware are always Microsoft's in the cloud.

q: Which items stay the customer's responsibility no matter whether the workload is IaaS, PaaS or SaaS?
opts: Information and data, devices, and accounts and identities
Physical hosts, physical network and datacenter
The operating system and runtime patching in every service model
Hypervisor security, host firmware and the physical servers beneath them
why: Data, devices and identities are always the customer's. Physical hosts, network and datacenter are always the provider's, and the operating system shifts depending on the model.

q: A security team puts a firewall at the perimeter, segments the network, enables MFA, encrypts data and locks the server room. Which concept does this describe?
why: Defense in depth uses several independent layers (physical, identity, perimeter, network, compute, application, data) so one failure does not expose everything. Zero Trust is about verifying every request, not about stacking layers.

q: Which statement matches the Zero Trust principle "assume breach"?
opts: Trust any request that originates from inside the corporate network by default
Segment access, encrypt data and monitor so damage from a compromise is limited
Grant administrators permanent standing access so routine work is faster
Verify a user once at the start of the day and trust the session afterwards
why: Assume breach means designing so that an attacker who gets in can do limited damage: segmentation, end-to-end encryption and analytics to detect threats. Trusting the internal network or granting standing access is the opposite.

q: A system must store user passwords so they can be checked at sign-in but never recovered if the database is stolen. Which technique fits?
opts: Symmetric encryption with a shared key
Asymmetric encryption with a public key
why: A salted hash is one-way, so the original password cannot be recovered from the database. Encryption is reversible by anyone holding the key, and Base64 is just an encoding, not protection.

q: Which describes asymmetric encryption?
opts: One shared secret key is used for both encrypting and decrypting
A public key and a private key form a linked pair
Data is converted into a fixed-length value that cannot be reversed
Data is encrypted only while stored on disk
why: Asymmetric encryption uses a key pair: what one key encrypts only the other can decrypt. A single shared key is symmetric, a fixed-length irreversible output is a hash, and "at rest" describes where data is, not the algorithm.

q: An auditor asks the team to show that policies are followed and evidence of the controls is kept. Which part of GRC is this?
why: Compliance is demonstrating adherence to laws, regulations and standards. Governance sets the rules and accountability, and risk is identifying and reducing what could go wrong.

q: A European retailer chooses to keep customer data only in Azure regions inside the EU, so local laws apply to that data. Which pair of terms applies?
opts: Data residency, with data sovereignty as the legal effect
Data sovereignty only, because residency is not relevant to the choice of region
Federation, with single sign-on as the legal effect
Hashing, with encryption as the resulting legal effect on stored data
why: Choosing the location is data residency; the fact that the laws of that location govern the data is data sovereignty. Federation and hashing are unrelated.

q: A user signs in with a password and approves a prompt in an app. A moment later the system checks that the user may open a specific document. Which two processes happened, in order?
why: The system first proves who the user is (authentication) and then decides what that identity is allowed to do (authorization). The order never reverses.

q: Which statement explains why identity is called the primary security perimeter?
opts: Firewalls no longer exist in cloud environments, so nothing else can be controlled
Users and data often sit outside the corporate network, so the verified identity is the key control
Passwords are impossible to steal once they are stored in the cloud
Only administrators have identities that need protecting in the cloud
why: When apps and data live in the cloud and people work from anywhere, the network edge no longer decides who gets in; the verified identity does. Firewalls still exist, and passwords are routinely stolen, which is why stronger methods matter.

q: Contoso employees sign in to a partner's web app with their own Contoso accounts, and the partner trusts Contoso's sign-in. What is this trust arrangement called?
why: Federation is a trust between identity providers so one authenticates users for the other's resources. Hashing, layered defense and data location are different concepts.

q: Microsoft Entra ID is the same product as on-premises Active Directory Domain Services, simply hosted in the cloud.
why: Entra ID is a cloud identity provider built around web protocols such as SAML, OpenID Connect and OAuth. AD DS is an on-premises directory built around Kerberos, NTLM, LDAP and domain controllers. They are often used together in hybrid identity.

q: Hashing is reversible if you hold the correct key.
why: Hashing is a one-way function with no key to reverse it. Reversibility with a key describes encryption.

q: Which two statements describe the Zero Trust model? (Choose two.)
opts: Verify explicitly using all available signals
Trust devices because they are on the internal network
Rely on a strong network perimeter as the main control
why: Verify explicitly and use least privilege access are two of the three principles (the third is assume breach). Trusting the internal network and leaning on the perimeter are the traditional model Zero Trust replaces.

q: Which two items are always the customer's responsibility in the shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)
why: Data and identities (along with devices) are always the customer's. The datacenter and the physical network are the provider's in a cloud service.

q: Which statement best describes Microsoft Entra ID?
opts: An on-premises directory service that runs only on Windows Server domain controllers
Microsoft's cloud-based identity and access management service
A managed firewall for filtering traffic between Azure virtual networks
A tool for classifying and labeling documents in Microsoft 365
why: Entra ID, formerly Azure Active Directory, is the cloud identity and access management service behind Microsoft 365 and Azure. Domain controllers belong to on-premises AD DS, firewalls to network security, and classification to Purview.

q: A web app running in Azure must read secrets from Azure Key Vault without any password stored in its code. Which identity type fits best?
why: A managed identity gives the app an automatically managed credential so no secret is stored. Guest accounts are for external people, groups collect identities, and devices are not used for app authentication.

q: Which statement about managed identities is correct?
opts: A system-assigned identity is created with, and deleted with, the Azure resource it belongs to
A user-assigned identity can only ever be used by exactly one Azure resource at a time
Managed identities require a client secret that must be stored in the app settings
Managed identities are intended only for human users who sign in interactively
why: System-assigned identities share the lifecycle of their resource. User-assigned identities are standalone and can be shared across resources, and the whole point of a managed identity is that no secret is stored.

q: A consultant from a partner company needs to access one SharePoint site using the consultant's own work account. Which Entra feature supports this?
opts: Entra Domain Services with a managed domain
B2B collaboration with a guest user
Password hash synchronization from Active Directory
why: B2B collaboration invites external people as guests who sign in with their own credentials. Domain Services provides managed AD DS, and the other options are unrelated to external collaboration.

q: A company has Active Directory on premises and wants users to keep one identity for Microsoft 365. Which approach provides this?
opts: Hybrid identity using Microsoft Entra Connect or Cloud Sync
Creating separate cloud accounts and distributing new passwords
Using Azure RBAC to copy users
why: Hybrid identity synchronizes on-premises accounts to Entra ID so users have a single identity. Separate accounts create the duplication hybrid identity avoids, and RBAC and security defaults do not sync identities.

q: Which hybrid authentication method validates user passwords directly against on-premises Active Directory at the time of sign-in?
why: Pass-through authentication checks the password against on-premises AD DS when the user signs in. Password hash synchronization validates against a synced hash in the cloud instead.

q: A laptop is owned by the company, joined directly to Microsoft Entra ID, and the user signs in with a work account. How is this device described?
why: Entra joined devices belong to the organization and sign in with work accounts. Registered means a personal device, and hybrid joined means joined to on-premises AD DS and registered with Entra ID.

q: Which Entra license tier is the lowest one that includes Conditional Access?
why: Conditional Access needs Entra ID P1. Risk-based conditions need P2 because they rely on ID Protection, and Free provides security defaults instead.

q: A workload identity can represent an application or a service, not just a person.
why: Entra ID supports identities for software, including app registrations, service principals and managed identities, so code can authenticate without borrowing a person's account.

q: Microsoft Entra Agent ID gives AI agents identities of their own instead of having them borrow a person's account.
why: Agent identities extend the workload identity idea to AI agents, so each agent can be governed, protected and audited separately from the people who use it.

q: A guest user in B2B collaboration must be given a new password in your tenant.
why: Guests authenticate with the credentials from their own home organization or identity provider, which is a key benefit of B2B collaboration.

q: Which two items are examples of workload identities? (Choose two.)
why: Managed identities and service principals represent software. A guest user is a person from outside, and a group is a collection used to assign access.

q: A user signs in with a password and then enters a code from an authenticator app. Which factors are combined?
opts: Something you know and something you have
Something you are and something you have
Something you are and something you know
why: The password is knowledge and the app or phone is possession. Two knowledge items would not be true multifactor authentication.

q: Which authentication method is considered passwordless and phishing-resistant?
opts: A code delivered by SMS text message
A passkey on a FIDO2 security key
A one-time code sent by email
why: Passkeys and FIDO2 keys use a device-held private key bound to the real site, so a fake site cannot capture a reusable secret. SMS, email codes and security questions can all be intercepted or guessed.

q: Which Windows feature replaces passwords with a PIN or biometric tied to the device?
opts: Entra Application Proxy for on-premises apps
why: Windows Hello for Business is a passwordless credential unlocked locally by PIN or biometrics. The others serve different purposes.

q: A small organization with no Conditional Access licenses wants a quick, free baseline that requires MFA registration and blocks legacy authentication. What should it enable?
why: Security defaults are free preconfigured settings that enforce MFA registration and block legacy authentication. PIM, access reviews and entitlement management are governance features that need higher licenses.

q: Users must be able to reset their own forgotten passwords, and the new password must flow back to on-premises AD DS. Which feature is needed beyond SSPR itself?
why: Password writeback sends a reset or change made in the cloud back to on-premises Active Directory. Smart lockout and banned lists protect against guessing and weak passwords but do not write back.

q: An organization wants to prevent users from choosing passwords that contain the company name. Which capability should it use?
opts: Custom banned password list in Microsoft Entra Password Protection
Conditional Access policies running in report-only mode
Registering devices in Microsoft Entra ID
why: Password Protection with a custom banned list blocks specified terms in addition to Microsoft's global banned list. The custom list requires P1.

q: Which statement about SMS and voice call authentication is accurate?
opts: They are the most phishing-resistant methods that Entra ID supports
They are supported MFA methods but weaker than the Authenticator app or passkeys
They are only available to guest users from partner organizations
They replace the need for a password entirely in every sign-in
why: Phone-based verification works as a second factor but can be intercepted or socially engineered, so stronger methods are preferred. They do not remove the password.

q: Using two different passwords for the same sign-in counts as multifactor authentication.
why: MFA needs factors from different categories, such as knowledge plus possession. Two passwords are both something you know.

q: With passkeys, the private key is sent to the website when you sign in.
why: The private key never leaves the device or security key. The device signs a challenge, and the service verifies it with the registered public key.

q: Which two are passwordless methods supported by Microsoft Entra ID? (Choose two.)
why: The Authenticator app and FIDO2 keys can sign a user in without a password. Security questions and long passwords are still knowledge-based secrets.

q: A policy states: if a user signs in from outside the corporate network to the finance app, require MFA. Which Entra feature enforces this?
why: Conditional Access evaluates signals such as location and app and applies controls such as requiring MFA. The others handle recertification, password quality and access bundles.

q: Before enforcing a new Conditional Access policy, an administrator wants to see which sign-ins it would have affected without blocking anyone. What should be used?
why: Report-only mode logs the policy's effect without enforcing it, which allows safe testing. Deleting the policy would show nothing, and security defaults are a separate baseline.

q: Which role would you assign so someone can create and manage Azure virtual machines in one resource group but not manage Entra users?
opts: Global Administrator for the whole tenant
An Azure RBAC role such as Contributor at the resource group scope
Privileged Role Administrator in Entra ID
why: Azure RBAC controls Azure resources and can be scoped to a resource group. Global Administrator, User Administrator and Privileged Role Administrator are Entra roles that govern the directory and carry far more power than needed.

q: Which statement correctly contrasts Entra roles with Azure RBAC roles?
opts: Entra roles manage directory resources such as users and policies; Azure RBAC manages Azure resources
Entra roles manage Azure virtual machines; Azure RBAC manages users and groups
They are identical and can be used interchangeably in any scenario
Azure RBAC only applies to Microsoft 365 mailboxes and nothing else
why: Entra roles are for the identity service itself, and Azure RBAC is for Azure resources. They use separate role sets and different scopes.

q: A company wants employees to reach internal web apps remotely without a traditional VPN, using identity-based, zero-trust access. Which Entra service fits?
why: Entra Private Access, part of Global Secure Access, provides identity-aware access to private apps instead of a network-wide VPN. Internet Access secures internet and SaaS traffic, which is the other half of the SSE solution.

q: Which Conditional Access result is the strictest?
why: Block access denies the request outright. The other results allow access, with or without extra requirements, or only log.

q: Conditional Access policies are evaluated after first-factor authentication has completed.
why: Conditional Access acts as a policy engine after the user passes the initial sign-in, then decides whether to allow, require more proof, or block.

q: A user who holds the Azure Owner role on a subscription automatically has the Entra Global Administrator role.
why: Azure RBAC and Entra roles are separate systems. Owning an Azure subscription does not grant directory administration, and the reverse is also true by default.

q: Which two signals can Conditional Access use in a policy? (Choose two.)
opts: The color of the user's monitor
why: Conditional Access signals include user or group, location, device, application and risk. The other items are not signals.

q: An organization needs managers to confirm every quarter which guests still need access to Teams. Which capability handles this?
why: Access reviews let designated reviewers recertify access on a schedule, and can remove access automatically. The others are authentication or publishing features.

q: A system administrator should only hold the Exchange Administrator role for a few hours when needed, after giving a justification. Which feature provides this?
why: PIM provides just-in-time, time-limited role activation with justification, approval and MFA options. It requires P2 or ID Governance.

q: In PIM, what does it mean when a user is "eligible" for a role?
opts: They hold the role permanently with no activation needed
They can activate the role when needed
They have been explicitly denied the role by an administrator
They are a guest user from an external organization
why: Eligible assignments must be activated, usually for a limited time. Active assignments are the ones in effect now.

q: Microsoft Entra ID Protection detects that a sign-in came from an anonymous IP address and an unfamiliar location. What is this an example of?
opts: A risk detection that contributes to sign-in risk
An access package request in entitlement management
A lifecycle workflow task for a new joiner
A system-assigned identity for an Azure resource
why: ID Protection flags suspicious sign-in behavior as risk detections that can feed risk-based Conditional Access. The other options belong to governance and workload identity.

q: Which license is required to use risk-based Conditional Access policies that react to sign-in risk?
opts: None, they are included in security defaults
why: Risk-based conditions rely on ID Protection, a P2 feature. P1 gives standard Conditional Access without risk signals.

q: A new employee starts Monday. The organization wants group membership, a welcome email and a Temporary Access Pass to be set up automatically. Which feature automates this?
opts: Access reviews of existing group members
Password writeback to on-premises AD DS
why: Lifecycle workflows automate joiner, mover and leaver tasks. Access reviews recertify existing access instead of provisioning it.

q: Which feature lets a user request a bundle of groups, apps and sites that expires automatically and can require manager approval?
opts: Security defaults for the whole tenant
why: Access packages in entitlement management bundle resources, approvals and expirations. They are an ID Governance capability.

q: Privileged Identity Management can require approval and a justification when a user activates a privileged role.
why: PIM supports approval, justification, MFA and time limits on activation, and keeps an audit history of activations.

q: Access reviews can only be performed by Global Administrators.
why: Reviewers can be resource owners, managers, group owners, selected reviewers or the users themselves, which is what makes recertification scale.

q: Which two are capabilities of Microsoft Entra ID Governance? (Choose two.)
opts: Blocking DDoS attacks on public IP addresses
Encrypting Azure Storage with customer-managed keys
why: Entitlement management and access reviews are core ID Governance features. DDoS Protection and storage encryption belong to Azure infrastructure security.

q: Which two features require Microsoft Entra ID P2 (or ID Governance)? (Choose two.)
why: PIM and ID Protection are P2 features. Basic SSO and security defaults are available without a paid tier.

q: An online store wants protection against attacks that flood its public website with traffic to make it unavailable, plus attack analytics. Which service fits?
why: DDoS Protection mitigates traffic floods and provides analytics. Bastion is for remote access, Key Vault stores secrets, and Audit records activity.

q: Which DDoS Protection tier provides cost protection and access to the DDoS Rapid Response team?
why: DDoS Network Protection adds Rapid Response support, cost protection and a WAF discount. IP Protection lacks those, and infrastructure protection is the free automatic baseline.

q: A company wants a central managed firewall for all outbound traffic from its virtual networks, with FQDN rules and threat intelligence filtering. Which service should it use?
why: Azure Firewall provides central, stateful filtering with FQDN rules and threat intelligence. NSGs are simpler subnet and NIC filters, Bastion is for remote access, and WAF is for inbound web attacks.

q: A regulated organization must inspect encrypted outbound traffic and detect intrusions with signatures. Which Azure Firewall SKU is required?
why: TLS inspection and IDPS are Premium features. Basic and Standard do not offer them.

q: A web application is being hit with SQL injection and cross-site scripting attempts. Which service defends against these?
opts: Network security groups on the subnet
why: WAF inspects HTTP and HTTPS requests at layer 7 for common web exploits. NSGs only filter by IP, port and protocol, so they cannot see SQL injection.

q: On which Azure services can Azure Web Application Firewall be deployed?
opts: Azure Application Gateway and Azure Front Door
Azure Bastion and Azure Key Vault only
Network security groups and user-defined route tables
Azure Monitor and Log Analytics workspaces
why: WAF is a feature of Application Gateway, Front Door and Azure CDN. The other pairs are unrelated services.

q: An NSG contains a custom rule with priority 300 that denies RDP (port 3389) from the internet and another custom rule with priority 400 that allows RDP from the internet. What happens to RDP traffic from the internet?
opts: It is denied, because the lower priority number is processed first
It is allowed, because the rule with the higher number takes precedence over the lower one
It is allowed, because allow rules are always evaluated before deny rules
The NSG rejects both rules as a conflict and drops all traffic
why: NSG rules are evaluated from the lowest to the highest priority number and processing stops at the first match, so the deny at 300 applies before the allow at 400 is ever considered.

q: To which two things can a network security group be associated?
opts: A subnet or a network interface
A storage account or a key vault
A management group or a subscription
A Microsoft Entra tenant or a domain
why: NSGs attach at the subnet level or to a VM's network interface. They do not attach to storage accounts, management groups or tenants.

q: An architect puts the web tier, application tier and database tier in separate subnets with rules that only allow the required traffic between them. Which security practice is this?
opts: Hashing of the data in each tier
Data residency in a single region
why: Splitting a network into isolated parts and controlling traffic between them is segmentation. It limits lateral movement after a breach.

q: Administrators need RDP and SSH access to Azure VMs from the Azure portal without giving the VMs public IP addresses. Which service provides this?
why: Bastion offers secure browser-based RDP and SSH over TLS directly to private VMs. Firewall filters traffic, and the others do not provide remote sessions.

q: A developer is storing a database connection string in a source code file. Which Azure service should hold it instead?
why: Key Vault is designed to store secrets, keys and certificates with access control and logging. The other products do not store secrets.

q: Which Azure service uses hardware security modules to help protect cryptographic keys?
opts: Azure Key Vault Premium or Managed HSM
Azure DDoS Protection on public IPs
why: Key Vault Premium and Managed HSM store keys in HSMs. The others have nothing to do with key storage.

q: Azure DDoS infrastructure protection for public IP addresses is included automatically at no extra cost.
why: Basic infrastructure protection applies to all Azure public IPs. The paid IP Protection and Network Protection tiers add tuning, analytics and support.

q: A network security group can detect SQL injection attacks inside HTTP requests.
why: NSGs filter on IP addresses, ports and protocols at layers 3 and 4. Application-layer attacks such as SQL injection need a web application firewall.

q: Which two statements about Azure Bastion are correct? (Choose two.)
opts: It provides RDP and SSH over TLS from the Azure portal
It lets VMs avoid public IP addresses for management
why: Bastion gives managed remote access and removes the need for public IPs on VMs. SQL injection protection is WAF and key storage is Key Vault.

q: Which two features are available only in Azure Firewall Premium? (Choose two.)
why: TLS inspection and IDPS are Premium. FQDN filtering and threat intelligence are available in lower SKUs as well.

q: A security team wants a single dashboard that shows misconfigured resources across Azure, AWS and Google Cloud with prioritized fixes. Which service fits?
why: Defender for Cloud assesses posture across multiple clouds and recommends fixes. Compliance Manager tracks regulatory assessments, and ID Protection is about identity risk.

q: What does cloud security posture management (CSPM) do?
opts: Detects and prioritizes misconfigurations and gives recommendations to harden resources
Stores encryption keys and secrets for applications
Replaces the need for network security groups and firewalls
Manages user passwords and sign-in methods
why: CSPM continuously assesses resources against standards and recommends fixes. Key storage is Key Vault, and passwords are an identity concern.

q: Which capability is part of the free Foundational CSPM in Defender for Cloud?
why: Secure score, recommendations and asset inventory are free. Attack path analysis, agentless scanning and cloud security explorer need the paid Defender CSPM plan.

q: What does a higher secure score in Defender for Cloud indicate?
opts: More security alerts have been raised in the period
More resources have been deployed in the subscription
Higher Azure costs for the subscription
why: Secure score reflects how many recommendations have been remediated. A higher score means fewer identified risks.

q: Which Defender for Cloud feature shows how an attacker could chain weaknesses to reach a critical asset?
why: Attack path analysis, a Defender CSPM feature, visualizes exploitable routes to critical resources so you can fix the riskiest first.

q: Which pair correctly pairs the two halves of Defender for Cloud?
opts: CSPM improves posture; cloud workload protection defends running workloads
CSPM runs automated playbooks; workload protection stores secrets and keys
CSPM scans email for phishing; workload protection scans mobile devices
CSPM classifies documents by sensitivity; workload protection retains them
why: CSPM finds and fixes misconfigurations, while Defender plans provide threat detection and protection for workloads such as servers, containers and databases.

q: The security team wants RDP and SSH ports on VMs closed by default and opened only temporarily on approved request. Which feature provides this?
opts: Just-in-time VM access in Defender for Servers
A custom banned password list in Entra
Safe Links in Defender for Office 365
why: JIT VM access locks management ports and opens them briefly on approval. The other options do not manage VM ports.

q: What is the Microsoft cloud security benchmark in Defender for Cloud?
opts: A built-in security standard that drives recommendations and secure score
A list of banned passwords maintained by Microsoft
A type of sensitivity label for documents
A Sentinel playbook that automates responses
why: The Microsoft cloud security benchmark is the default standard Defender for Cloud assesses resources against.

q: Defender for Cloud can assess resources in AWS and Google Cloud as well as Azure.
why: Defender for Cloud provides multicloud coverage once those accounts and projects are connected.

q: Which two capabilities require the paid Defender CSPM plan rather than Foundational CSPM? (Choose two.)
why: Attack path analysis and agentless scanning are paid features. Secure score and asset inventory are part of the free tier.

q: Which description best matches a SIEM?
opts: It collects and correlates security data from many sources and raises alerts
It encrypts data at rest in storage accounts
It authenticates users with passkeys and security keys
why: A SIEM aggregates logs and events, detects threats through correlation and supports investigation. The others describe encryption, identity and information protection.

q: In Microsoft Sentinel, which component automates responses to incidents, such as disabling a compromised user?
opts: Playbooks built on Azure Logic Apps
why: Playbooks are automated workflows that implement SOAR. Workbooks visualize, connectors ingest and bookmarks save hunting results.

q: An analyst writes KQL queries to look for suspicious activity that no existing rule has flagged. Which Sentinel capability is this?
why: Hunting is proactive, query-driven searching for threats. Analytics rules would be automated detections.

q: Which Sentinel feature builds a baseline of normal behavior to flag anomalous user activity?
why: UEBA models typical behavior of users and entities and highlights deviations.

q: What does SOAR stand for and what does it do?
opts: Security orchestration, automation and response; it automates incident handling
Secure operating access resource; it grants permissions
Security operations audit record; it stores audit logs
Single-sign-on application registry; it lists apps
why: SOAR automates and orchestrates responses to security events, which in Sentinel is done with playbooks and automation rules.

q: Where is Microsoft Sentinel moving to be supported exclusively according to Microsoft's current guidance?
why: Microsoft states Sentinel will be available only in the Defender portal after March 31, 2027.

q: Microsoft Sentinel is both a SIEM and a SOAR solution.
why: Sentinel collects and analyzes security data (SIEM) and can automate response with playbooks and automation rules (SOAR).

q: Which two Sentinel elements are used to bring data in and to visualize it? (Choose two.)
why: Connectors ingest data and workbooks provide dashboards. Passkeys and sensitivity labels are unrelated.

q: Which Microsoft solution correlates alerts from endpoints, identities, email and cloud apps into a single incident?
why: Defender XDR unifies detection and response across Microsoft workloads and groups related alerts into incidents.

q: Employees receive emails with links to fake sign-in pages. Which product checks links when users click them?
why: Safe Links verifies URLs at the time of click. Vulnerability Management finds software weaknesses, and Defender for Identity watches Active Directory.

q: Which Defender for Office 365 feature opens email attachments in a sandbox before delivery?
why: Safe Attachments detonates files in a protected environment to find malware.

q: A security team wants to run phishing simulation training for employees. Which product plan includes this?
why: Attack simulation training is part of Defender for Office 365 Plan 2.

q: Which product provides endpoint detection and response (EDR) for Windows, macOS, Linux and mobile devices?
why: Defender for Endpoint is the endpoint security platform with EDR, attack surface reduction and next-generation antivirus.

q: Which Defender product acts as a cloud access security broker and finds unsanctioned SaaS apps used by employees?
why: Defender for Cloud Apps provides Cloud Discovery for shadow IT and is Microsoft's CASB.

q: Which product detects pass-the-hash and lateral movement attacks using signals from domain controllers?
why: Defender for Identity uses sensors on domain controllers to detect on-premises identity attacks such as pass-the-hash.

q: A team needs a prioritized list of vulnerable software across devices, based on threat intelligence and business context. Which solution provides it?
why: Defender Vulnerability Management discovers weaknesses and prioritizes remediation by risk.

q: Which Defender portal capability shows whether an emerging threat affects your organization and whether protections are in place?
why: Threat analytics reports from Microsoft Threat Intelligence are combined with your own data to show exposure.

q: What is the purpose of attack surface reduction rules in Defender for Endpoint?
opts: To block risky behaviors that malware commonly uses
To manage guest users and their access
why: ASR rules prevent behaviors such as Office apps launching child processes.

q: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps and Microsoft Defender for Cloud are the same product.
why: Defender for Cloud Apps is a CASB for SaaS apps. Defender for Cloud protects Azure, multicloud and hybrid infrastructure and workloads.

q: Defender for Identity protects identities in on-premises Active Directory.
why: It uses sensors on domain controllers and similar servers to detect attacks on AD DS identities.

q: Which two products are components of Microsoft Defender XDR? (Choose two.)
why: Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Identity are among the XDR services, along with Office 365 and Cloud Apps. Bastion and Key Vault are Azure services.

q: Which two are Defender for Cloud Apps capabilities? (Choose two.)
opts: Discovering shadow IT with Cloud Discovery
Applying session controls with Conditional Access app control
why: Cloud Discovery and session controls are core CASB capabilities. Patching domain controllers and disk encryption are not.

q: An auditor asks for Microsoft's ISO 27001 certificate and SOC reports for Azure. Where can you find these?
why: The Service Trust Portal hosts audit reports, certifications and compliance documentation. The others are security and identity management tools.

q: Which Microsoft privacy principle states that customer email, chat and files are not used for advertising targeting?
opts: Benefits to you from data collected
Control over how data is used
why: No content-based targeting means Microsoft does not use what is in your content to target ads. Control and transparency concern choices and clarity, and benefits to you concern value in return for data.

q: Which of these is NOT one of Microsoft's six privacy principles?
why: The six principles are control, transparency, security, strong legal protections, no content-based targeting and benefits to you. Monetizing customer content contradicts them.

q: The Service Trust Portal provides audit reports and compliance documentation about Microsoft cloud services.
why: It is the central location for audit reports, certifications, compliance guides and whitepapers.

q: An organization wants templates and step-by-step improvement actions to help it comply with GDPR. Which tool should it use?
opts: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on devices
why: Compliance Manager provides assessments for regulations and improvement actions with guidance. The others do not track regulatory compliance.

q: What does the compliance score in Compliance Manager measure?
opts: The number of users licensed in the organization
The amount of data stored in SharePoint sites
Whether the organization is legally compliant
why: The score reflects completed improvement actions, helping you prioritize work. It is not a legal certification of compliance.

q: In Compliance Manager, who can perform improvement actions?
opts: Microsoft for some actions and the customer for others
Only Microsoft can perform any of the actions
Only the customer can perform any of the actions
Only external auditors can perform the actions
why: Some improvement actions are managed by Microsoft and others by the customer; both contribute to the score.

q: A high compliance score guarantees that an organization meets all legal obligations.
why: The score is a guide to progress on improvement actions. It does not constitute a guarantee or certification of compliance.

q: Which two items are part of Compliance Manager? (Choose two.)
why: Assessments and improvement actions are core. Safe Attachments belongs to Defender for Office 365 and Cloud Discovery to Defender for Cloud Apps.

q: A compliance team wants to find documents that contain credit card numbers anywhere in the organization. Which Purview capability identifies them?
opts: Safe Links in Defender for Office 365
Access reviews in Entra ID Governance
why: Sensitive information types detect patterns such as credit card numbers. The others belong to other solutions.

q: The team needs to see a list of where labeled or sensitive items currently exist and, for authorized users, view their content. Which tool provides this?
why: Content explorer gives a current view of classified items. Activity explorer shows what happened to them over time.

q: Which tool shows a history of actions on labeled content, such as when a label was changed or a file was copied?
why: Activity explorer provides a timeline of labeling and handling activities.

q: Which feature adds encryption and a "Confidential" watermark that stays with a document when it is emailed outside the company?
why: Sensitivity labels can encrypt and mark content, and the protection follows the file.

q: Administrators created a sensitivity label, but users do not see it in Word. What is most likely missing?
opts: A sensitivity label policy publishing the label to the users
A data loss prevention policy for email
An access review of group members
why: Labels become available to users only after they are published through a label policy.

q: A policy must block users from emailing documents that contain social security numbers to outside recipients, showing a policy tip first. Which solution fits?
why: DLP detects sensitive content and enforces actions such as policy tips and blocking sharing.

q: Which feature prevents sensitive files from being copied to a USB drive on company laptops?
why: Endpoint DLP monitors and restricts actions on sensitive files on Windows and macOS devices.

q: A law requires all Exchange mailboxes to be kept for seven years and then deleted. What is the simplest approach?
opts: A retention policy applied to Exchange mailboxes
A sensitivity label applied to each individual email
Manually tagging every email with a retention label
Enabling security defaults in Entra ID
why: A retention policy applies automatically to every item in a location. Per-item tagging is slower and unnecessary for a blanket rule.

q: Which statement best distinguishes a retention label from a retention policy?
opts: A label is applied to individual items and can declare a record; a policy applies to whole locations
A label applies to whole locations; a policy is applied to single items and records
They are identical and the terms can be used interchangeably
A label only encrypts files and has no retention settings
why: Labels are item-level and can mark content as a record. Policies apply broadly to the locations they target.

q: An organization needs documents that cannot be edited or deleted for the duration of their retention period, with proof of disposal at the end. Which capability fits?
why: Records management uses retention labels to lock content as a record and supports disposition review with proof of deletion.

q: A sensitivity label can apply encryption that stays with the file.
why: Label protection settings include encryption and access control that persist with the content.

q: Retention policies must be applied by each user to every individual document.
why: Retention policies are applied by administrators to locations, so users do not tag documents themselves. Item-level labels are the option users can apply.

q: Which two actions can a DLP policy take when it detects sensitive content? (Choose two.)
opts: Show a policy tip to the user
Join the device to the domain
why: DLP can warn users with policy tips, block, allow justified overrides and raise alerts. The others are unrelated.

q: Which two are used by Purview to classify data? (Choose two.)
why: SITs and trainable classifiers identify content. NSGs and Safe Links belong to network and email security.

q: A company wants to detect employees who copy large amounts of files to personal cloud storage shortly before they resign. Which solution fits?
why: Insider risk management uses indicators and policy templates such as data theft by departing users to raise alerts.

q: How does insider risk management help protect user privacy?
opts: Usernames are pseudonymized by default and access is role-based
It never records any user activity at all
It publishes every alert to all employees for transparency
It disables auditing for the monitored users
why: Privacy is built in through pseudonymization and role-based access to alerts and cases.

q: Legal counsel needs to preserve and collect mailbox and file content for a lawsuit, placing a hold on it. Which Purview solution is used?
why: eDiscovery lets you create cases, place legal holds, search, review and export content.

q: Which eDiscovery edition adds custodian management, review sets and near-duplicate detection?
why: Premium extends Standard with custodians, review sets and advanced analytics for complex cases.

q: An investigator needs to find who deleted a file in SharePoint last month. Which solution provides this?
why: Audit records user and admin activities so you can search for who did what and when.

q: Which feature distinguishes Audit (Premium) from Audit (Standard)?
opts: Audit log retention policies and longer retention
Being able to search audit logs at all
Being turned on by default for the tenant
Exporting audit records to a CSV file
why: Premium adds retention policies, one-year default retention for key services and up to 10 years with an add-on. The other items exist in both.

q: What is the default audit log retention for Audit (Standard)?
why: Audit (Standard) keeps records for 180 days. Longer retention needs Audit (Premium) and the right licensing.

q: Insider risk management is designed mainly to stop external attackers who have no access to the organization.
why: It focuses on risky activity by people who already have legitimate access, such as employees and contractors.

q: eDiscovery can place a legal hold so that content is preserved while a case is investigated.
why: Holds preserve content, even if users try to delete it, while the matter is open.

q: Which two are Audit (Premium) capabilities? (Choose two.)
why: Premium adds retention policies and high-value events. The other options are not audit features.

q: Which two solutions sit under Microsoft Purview? (Choose two.)
why: Both are Purview solutions. Bastion is an Azure networking service and Entra Connect is identity synchronization.
